# Rikugan (六眼)

> A reverse-engineering agent that lives inside IDA Pro 9.3 and Binary Ninja as a native C++ plugin (Linux, macOS, Windows). Its agent — turn loop, every model provider and login, sessions, compaction, retries, skills, MCP, file/shell/search tools — is libomc (oh-my-c), linked in-process (on Windows: libomc.dll beside the plugin). Rikugan adds the host analysis tools, the Qt chat panel, per-database chats, undo, plan/explore/modify/research modes, subagents with host tools, the bulk renamer, analysis profiles, and the RE prompts and skills. Rikugan 1.x was a Python plugin; it remains only in the git history.

## Documentation

- [README.md](README.md): install, features, providers.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): developer guide — layout, building, how a chat works, adding tools, threading and security rules.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): internals — libomc embedding, threads, chat lifecycle, system prompt, tool pipeline, undo, modes, subagents, bulk renamer, settings, AuthSync, security model.
- [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md): build trees, Qt headers, submodules and BN ABI pinning, tests, adding tools/skills/prompts, releases.
- [prompts/MANIFEST.md](prompts/MANIFEST.md): every model-facing text and its placeholders.
- [Docs page](https://rikugan.reversing.codes/docs.html) and [Architecture page](https://rikugan.reversing.codes/ARCHITECTURE.html).

## Key Concepts

- **libomc**: the agent runs in-process; Rikugan talks to it with omc's RPC frames (`omc_send` / event callback), one omc session plus one worker thread per chat (`src/common/omc/OmcSession.h`).
- **Host tools**: Rikugan's tools are registered with omc through `set_host_tools`; omc emits `host_tool_call`, Rikugan answers `host_tool_result`. Mutating and script tools are exclusive (run alone, in order).
- **Tool pipeline** (`ToolDispatcher::execute`): profile denial → mode phase gate → decompiler requirement → script approval → mutation approval → undo pre-state → run (host main thread when required) → mutation record → result cache → injection-marker strip → IOC filter → artifact cap.
- **Threads**: the host UI thread never waits; frames reach it through `EventQueue` (one coalesced event per burst); tool calls run on an 8-thread pool; SDK calls are marshalled to the host main thread.
- **Chats**: per database (`~/.rikugan/sessions/<db id>/chats.json`), resumed from omc session files; at most 4 live omc sessions per process.
- **Undo**: `/undo [N]` reverses renames, comments and prototypes; type, patch and IL/microcode tools are recorded as irreversible.
- **Memory**: `RIKUGAN.md` next to the database (`save_memory`), first 200 lines in the system prompt.
- **Security**: tool output is sanitised (injection markers, optional IOC redaction); scripts always ask; disk and shell tools only after the user allows them; omc's cwd is a scratch dir, project config and project MCP are off.

## File Layout

```
CMakeLists.txt     RIKUGAN_HOST = binja | ida | none (tests)
cmake/             omc.cmake + build_omc.sh / build_omc_win.cmake (libomc), embed.cmake (skills/ + prompts/ into the plugin)
prompts/           model-facing texts (MANIFEST.md)
skills/            12 built-in skills
src/common/        omc/ agent/ tools/ host/ security/ config/ ui/ util/
src/binja/         Plugin.cpp, host/ (BnHost, BnPython), tools/
src/ida/           sdk/Plugin.cpp, host/ (IdaHost, tools/), sdk/ (SDK subclasses, -fno-rtti)
tests/native/      QtTest suite against omc's mock model
tests/ida/         idalib tool test
third_party/       binaryninja-api, ida-sdk (submodules)
tools/             fetch_qt.sh / fetch_qt.ps1 (Qt headers matching each host), vsenv.ps1 (MSVC environment)
build.sh build.ps1 build and package the plugins into dist/
install.sh install.ps1  install a release (or dist/) into the hosts' plugins folders
```

## Commands

| Input | Description |
|---|---|
| `/plan <msg>` | Plan, approve, execute step by step |
| `/explore <msg>` | Read-only autonomous exploration with findings |
| `/modify <msg>` | Explore → plan → execute patches → save or discard |
| `/research <msg>` | Explore, then write Obsidian-style notes next to the database |
| `/undo [N]` | Undo the last N database changes |
| `/memory`, `/mcp`, `/doctor` | Show memory, MCP servers, setup diagnosis |
| `/<skill> args` | Run a skill (omc `/skill:<skill>`); `mode:` skills start their mode |
| `/compact`, `/retry`, `/model`, `/effort` | omc's commands |

## Built-in Skills

`/malware-analysis`, `/linux-malware`, `/deobfuscation` (plan mode), `/vuln-audit`, `/driver-analysis`, `/ctf`, `/generic-re`, `/ida-scripting`, `/binja-scripting`, `/modify` (exploration mode), `/smart-patch-ida`, `/smart-patch-binja`. User skills: `~/.rikugan/omc/agent/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`.

## Adding a Tool

```cpp
registry.add(rk::ToolSpec{
    "jump_to", "navigation", "Jump to the specified address.",
    {rk::ToolParam{"address", rk::ToolParam::String, "Target address (hex string, e.g. '0x401000')"}},
    rk::MainThread, 20000,
    [this](rk::ToolCall& call) {
        const uint64_t ea = call.address("address");
        ...
        return rk::ToolResult::ok(QStringLiteral("Jumped to %1").arg(rk::hex(ea)));
    }});
```

Added in the host's `registerTools()` (`src/binja/tools/`, `src/ida/host/tools/`). Every `Mutating` tool must be reversible in `MutationLog` or listed as known irreversible.

## Adding a Skill

`skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name: <slug>`, `description:`, optional `mode: plan | exploration`, then the instructions. Rebuild: skills are embedded in the plugin.
